lessons.culture: In Cairo a flat is often found through a broker (simsaar) or a sign on the building, and rent is quoted per month in pounds. A deposit (ta2meen) is common, water and electricity are usually paid separately by meter, and the lease should be written and signed before any money is paid.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "How many bedrooms does it have?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo a room is 'oDa' and 'kaam' comes before the noun.

exercises.tip: 'oDa' (plural 'oweD') is the Cairo word for a room; 'ghurfa' is bookish.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want a one-year lease"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say '3aayiz' (a woman: '3ayza').

exercises.tip: 'le-sana' means for a year.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Is there a lift?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo the lift is 'asanseer'.

exercises.tip: 'feeh' means there is; 'asanseer' is the everyday word for a lift.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "How much is the monthly rent?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'kaam ... fish-shahr'.

exercises.tip: Rent is quoted per month, in pounds (ginee).

exercises.prompt: Which one asks whether water and electricity are included?

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'dakhleen fil-eegaar' (inside the rent).

exercises.tip: 'shamleen' (included) is also understood, but 'dakhleen fil-eegaar' is what people say.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "I am looking for a flat to rent"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'badawwar 3ala'.

exercises.tip: 'badawwar 3ala' means I am looking for; ق in 'sha22a' is a hamza in Cairo.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "It is on the second floor"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo a floor is 'door'.

exercises.tip: 'door' is a floor; the ground floor is 'el-door el-ardi'.

exercises.prompt: فِيهَا كَام ___ نُوم؟  (How many bedrooms does it have?)
exercises.tip: 'oDet noom' is a bedroom, literally a sleep room.

exercises.prompt: اتْفَضَّل، دِي ___ الشَّقَّة  (Here are the keys of the flat)
exercises.tip: A single key is 'moftaaH'.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "الإِيجَار كَام فِي الشَّهْر؟". Say: five thousand pounds a month.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'khamas talaaf'.

exercises.tip: 'khamas talaaf' is five thousand in everyday Cairene.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فِيه أَسَانْسِير؟". Say: yes, the building has a lift.
exercises.tip: 'el-3imaara' is the apartment building.

dialogue.english: No problem, fix it and I will take the flat

pair.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?
Where do I put the fridge?

lessons.culture: A flat in Cairo is described by its bedrooms, then the rooms for guests and sitting, the kitchen and the bathrooms. It may be rented furnished or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where is the kitchen?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'feen' comes last.

exercises.tip: 'feen' (where) closes the question in Cairo.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Is the flat furnished?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo a question needs no 'hal', only the rising tone.

exercises.tip: Say it with a rising tone; no 'hal' is needed.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "There is a sofa in the living room"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'kanaba' for sofa.

exercises.tip: 'kanaba' is a sofa; 'oDet el-2o3aad' can also be called 'el-ma3eesha' or 'es-Saala'.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "How many bathrooms are in the flat?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'feeha kaam 7ammaam'.

exercises.tip: After 'kaam' the noun is singular: 'kaam 7ammaam'.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where do I put the fridge?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'tallaaga'.

exercises.tip: 'tallaaga' is a fridge.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Put the table here"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'tarabeeza' for a table.

exercises.tip: To a woman: '7oTTi'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "The bedroom is spacious"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'oDa' not 'ghurfa'.

exercises.tip: 'waas3a' agrees with 'oDa', which is feminine.

exercises.prompt: ___ فِين؟  (Where is the wardrobe?)

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'doolaab'.

exercises.tip: 'doolaab' is a wardrobe or cupboard.

exercises.prompt: التَّكْيِيف ___؟  (Does the air conditioner work?)
exercises.tip: A woman or a feminine thing: 'shaghghaala'. 'shaghghaal' means working.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "المَطْبَخ فِين؟". Say: next to the living room.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'ganb'.

exercises.tip: 'ganb' means next to.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فِيهَا كَام حَمَّام؟". Say: two bathrooms.
exercises.tip: The ending -een means exactly two: '7ammaameen'.

lessons.culture: A small repair is often done first by a relative or neighbour, and a plumber (sabbaak) or electrician (kahrabaa2i) is called for bigger jobs; it is polite to ask the price before the work starts. The helper is thanked with a du'a such as jazaaka Allaahu khayran, and people say al-7amdu lillaah when the job ends well.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The tap is leaking water"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo a tap is '7anafeyya' and it 'betnaqqaT' (drips).

exercises.tip: '7anafeyya' is the Cairo word for a tap; 'betnizz' also means it seeps.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where is the toolbox?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes put 'feen' last.

exercises.tip: '3edda' means the set of tools.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Pass me the screwdriver"?
exercises.tip: 'naawelni' is hand me; 'haatli' is bring me.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "The power is out in the house"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo the power 'cuts': 'kahraba 2ata3it'.

exercises.tip: People also say 'en-noor 2ata3'.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says "شُكْرًا، اشْتَغَلِت دِلْوَقْتِي". What do you answer?
exercises.tip: al-7amdu lillaah is fixed wording, the same in every dialect.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "I need a hammer and nails"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'shaakoosh' for a hammer.

exercises.tip: 'shaakoosh' is the everyday word for a hammer; a woman says 'me7taaga'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "The door does not close well"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'mish' is the negative and 'betqefel' is closes.

exercises.tip: 'mish' makes a verb or adjective negative.

exercises.prompt: اللَّمْبَة مِش ___  (The bulb does not work)
exercises.tip: 'shaghghaala' is feminine because 'lamba' is feminine.

exercises.prompt: كَلِّم ___ لَوْ لَازِم  (Call the plumber if needed)
exercises.tip: 'sabbaak' is a plumber; 'kahrabaa2i' is an electrician.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تِقْدَر تِصَلَّحُه؟". Say: yes, I will try.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'aywa, haHaawel'.

exercises.tip: 'ha-' before a verb makes it future.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "التَّكْلِفَة كَام؟". Say: I think not much.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'mish kiteer' (not much).

exercises.tip: 'mish kiteer' is not much.

phrases.arabic: إِحْنَا سَاكْنِين فِي الشَّقَّة اللِّي جَنْبُكُم
مُمْكِن تِسْتَلِم الجَوَابَات بِتَاعْتِنَا وَإِحْنَا مُسَافْرِين؟

pair.english: Which flat do you live in?
Where do we put the rubbish?

response.english: In the bin in front of the building

lessons.culture: Neighbours (geeraan) are close in Egypt: they send each other plates of food, visit when someone is ill, and many buildings have a doorman (bawwaab) who helps with mail and rubbish. Sending a dish to the new family next door is a common way to begin the friendship.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We are your new neighbours"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'e7na' and 'gedaad'.

exercises.tip: 'e7na' is we; 'gedaad' is the Cairo plural of new.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where do we put the rubbish?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'zibaala'.

exercises.tip: 'zibaala' is rubbish.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "I brought you some food"?

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'gebtilkom'.

exercises.tip: 'gebtilkom' already means I brought you (plural).

exercises.prompt: Which one means "A neighbour has a right over us"?
options: إِحْنَا سَاكْنِين فِي الشَّقَّة اللِّي جَنْبُكُم

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; in Cairo 'leeh' replaces 'li-'.

exercises.tip: 'leeh 7a22' means has a right.

exercises.prompt: You bring food to a neighbour and he answers with a blessing. Which one?

too_formal.feedback: Also correct and a fixed du'a shared by all dialects; 'teslam eedak' is the everyday Cairo thanks for food.

exercises.tip: To a woman: 'teslam eedik'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Which flat do you live in?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'enta saakin fi anhi sha22a'.

exercises.tip: To a woman: 'enti saakna fi anhi sha22a?'.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: "Could you move your car, please?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'momken' and 'law samaHt'.

exercises.tip: 'momken' (is it possible) starts a polite request.

exercises.prompt: مُمْكِن أَسْتَلِّف ___؟  (May I borrow a ladder?)
exercises.tip: 'sellem' is a ladder; it is also the word for a staircase.

exercises.prompt: آسِف عَلَى ___  (Sorry for the noise)
exercises.tip: A woman says 'aasfa'. 'dawsha' is noise and fuss.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "آسِف عَلَى الدَّوْشَة". Say: don't worry.

too_formal.feedback: Correct and kind; in Cairo 'wala yehemmak' is the usual one.

exercises.tip: 'wala yehemmak' means it doesn't matter, don't worry.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تَعَالَى اشْرَب مَعَانَا شَاي". Say: God willing, another time.

too_formal.item: إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّه، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر
too_formal.feedback: Correct Fusha; Cairenes say 'marra taanya'.

exercises.tip: 'marra taanya' is another time.

challenge.title: Viewing a Flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines where you ask about a flat to rent: the number of bedrooms, the floor, the monthly rent and whether water and electricity are included. Ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say what you decide. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 18.
required_elements: A question about the rent or the number of bedrooms using كام, such as الإيجار كام or فيها كام أوضة نوم.
A question about the floor, the lift, or whether water and electricity are included.
A request to see the flat using أقدر أشوف.
A question about the kitchen or the furniture using فين or مفروشة.
A closing decision with هاخدها or عايز عقد إيجار.
